name: Forgotten Genius
niche: The forgotten people behind inventions we use every day - especially scholars of the Islamic Golden Age, China, India - told as adventure stories.
audience: English-speaking, US-first, 18-55, curious; faceless animated explainer viewers
format: Hook with a concrete vivid question in the first 10 s -> 5-7 beats, each a mini-story with a visual mechanism -> twist -> short recap. Never dry lists.
honesty: Only verifiable history and physics. Numbers need a real source; disputed claims get ONE honest hedge. Never invent quotes or statistics. Avoid human-evolution claims (say 'hunters of the Ice Age', not 'early humans evolved'), avoid glorifying idols, pagan rituals, magic or superstition; if a past belief matters mention it briefly and neutrally as what people did, without endorsing. No nudity, no sexual topics, no gore beyond a factual mention.
character: the scholar, a young man in a long sand-coloured robe and a simple turban, carrying a notebook, round head, dot eyes
character_w: a young woman in a long modest dress and a plain headscarf
notes: New channel 2026-11 (bought account; 7-day warm-up before renaming/uploading). Proof: history-of-science channels; Golden Age stories are underserved (Muslim and general audience)
